clue.text: Flower, say, in black container

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it, so the word for speaking goes inside the rest

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
to say is to utter
a cup is a container

explanation.surface: A flower, say, standing in a black vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower, say' looks like one phrase, but 'say' belongs to the wordplay and sits inside B and CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow wild flower of meadows.

clue.text: Feel miserable when not on deck?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split into two words: to be down in spirits
second meaning: in the lower part of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if they feel seasick only when stuck in the cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as BE LOW, the word means to feel miserable; whole, it is the sailor's word for under the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, anything beneath the deck is said to be below, and being low means being sad.

clue.text: Provides accommodation for kids

definitions.meaning: second meaning: deceives, fools (a verb, not children)

explanation.surface: A foster carer who houses children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' reads as children being housed, but it is a verb meaning fools.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in lodgers is to house them; to take someone in is also to trick or deceive them.

clue.text: Grub for which Cockney uses microwave?

indicators.note: Cockney speech famously drops the h at the start of words, so the opening letter is lost

parts.note: a microwave oven is used to heat food

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks what food goes in the microwave.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney says 'eats' for HEATS by dropping the H; Cockney is the working-class London accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub and eats are both informal slang words for food.

clue.text: Ship's company sounded cocky?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sailors working a vessel
second meaning: an old past tense of crow, what a cockerel did

explanation.surface: A boastful-sounding group of sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocky' suggests arrogance, but it means like a cock: the cockerel crew, an old past tense of crowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The crew are the people who work a ship, and crew is an archaic past tense of crow.

clue.text: Very different — like those in Cracow and those in Gdansk?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: utterly opposed, as far apart as the earth's two ends

definitions.text: like those in Cracow and those in Gdansk
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: people of Poland living at a distance from each other

explanation.surface: Residents of two Polish cities are said to have little in common.
explanation.walkthrough: Cracow is in southern Poland and Gdansk on the northern coast, so their citizens are literally Poles some way apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely opposite, like the North and South Poles of the globe.

clue.text: Extra snake almost died

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word for snake loses its final letter

parts.note: an adder is a venomous snake
d is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: An additional snake was close to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Added means additional or extra, as in added sugar.

clue.text: Cherished desire possibly revealed to Parisian

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements the letters might take

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses a secret longing to a person from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiration is a hope or ambition that a person holds dear.

clue.text: One putting clothes on kitchen sideboard

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who clothes someone, as in theatre
second meaning: a cupboard with shelves for crockery

explanation.surface: Someone laying clothes out on a kitchen sideboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre dresser helps actors into costume, and a dresser is also a shelved kitchen cabinet.

clue.text: Gorgeous creature taking one's temperature is deceptive

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: An attractive person who takes your temperature is not to be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' just joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dishonest is untruthful, so deceptive is a close synonym.

clue.text: Be pleased with those who applaud quickly

parts.note: to like something is to be pleased with it
people who clap are clappers

explanation.surface: Enjoy the applause of the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Like the clappers is British slang for very fast, the clappers being the tongues of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British idiom means at great speed, as in running like the clappers.

clue.text: Insect that used to be quiet

parts.note: past tense of be
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: An insect that once was silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasp is a striped stinging insect.

clue.text: Initially Evening Standard journalists love coffee

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the next two words

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words
the press is journalists collectively
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Reporters at the Evening Standard, a London newspaper, adore their coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The Evening Standard is a London newspaper, which makes the journalists look like part of its staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is a strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Having an object, I have to follow Ford van

parts.note: the Transit is a Ford van model
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone who has something to carry must drive behind a Ford van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' places the contraction after the van's name.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a transitive verb is one that takes a direct object.

clue.text: Jack Sprat wouldn't talk

parts.note: surface reading: the nursery-rhyme man who could eat no fat refused to do something
setter's reading: the rhyme says he ate no fat, so he would not literally munch the greasy part of meat

explanation.surface: Jack Sprat refuses to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Jack Sprat could eat no fat; the idiom for chatting idly literally describes what he avoided.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal idiom means to chat at length in a relaxed way, i.e. to gossip.

clue.text: Something one has to have when pro is in a mess?

indicators.note: a mess is a state of disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about what a professional must possess when things go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: before you can have a thing, you must own it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is possession, the state that lets a person have and hold something.

clue.text: Photo sent out immediately

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order, as in put out

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A picture is dispatched without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at once, without any delay, as in fired on the spot.

clue.text: Wrong end of Dundee cake

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: end of picks only the final letter of the following place name

parts.note: the final letter of the Scottish city

explanation.surface: Someone has been served the wrong end of a Dundee cake, a Scottish fruit cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dundee cake' is a real Scottish fruit cake, which tempts you to read the phrase as one item.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich, layered continental cake.

clue.text: Giant bird a non-starter

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
taken as written

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A huge bird that never gets off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-starter' reads as a failure, but it splits into the word non and its starter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were giants of Greek myth, so a titan is any person or thing of great size.

clue.text: Quaver from end of anthem held by singer

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano

indicators.note: end of keeps only the last letter of the hymn word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A choirboy holds a wavering note at the end of the anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quaver' looks like the musical note, keeping up the choir picture, but here it is a verb meaning shake.
explanation.definitionFit: To quaver is to shake or quiver, especially of a voice, which is to tremble.

clue.text: Garfunkel recording that's seen in gallery?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read playfully: a piece produced by the singer Art Garfunkel
second meaning: a painting or sculpture on display

explanation.surface: An album by Art Garfunkel is displayed in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Art Garfunkel is the singer of Simon & Garfunkel, so a recording of his is a work of Art.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting or sculpture hung in a gallery is a creative piece of fine art.

clue.text: Airman coming from Scandinavia to Russia

indicators.note: coming from says the letters emerge out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the run of letters straddling these words

explanation.surface: A pilot flies in from northern Europe to Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, someone who flies aircraft.

clue.text: I mention sound or vision

indicators.note: sound tells you to judge the words by how they are pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: the pronoun is pronounced like the organ of vision
to mention is to cite, which is pronounced like sight

explanation.surface: A speaker lists the senses: hearing or seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound or vision' looks like a pair of senses, but 'sound' is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, i.e. vision.

clue.text: Walk with difficulty, having wilted?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to hobble
second meaning: an adjective, floppy and lacking firmness

explanation.surface: Someone droops and staggers along, exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: To limp is to walk unevenly from injury; limp also describes a drooping plant or lettuce.

clue.text: Thrash tense European

parts.note: the past is a grammatical tense
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A nervous European gives someone a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective meaning nervous, but it is the grammatical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To paste someone is informal British slang for beating them soundly.

clue.text: Firm American lawyer closing bars

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
a DA is a district attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A determined US attorney is shutting down drinking establishments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective and 'bars' like pubs; both shift meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music, its final measures.

clue.text: Part of church any parishioners should examine at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Churchgoers are urged to inspect part of their church.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the vaulted, often semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: New boots lift chap up — they're made for walking!

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into something fresh, a different order

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Fresh footwear gives a man a boost, echoing the song These Boots Are Made for Walkin'.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on Nancy Sinatra's song These Boots Are Made for Walkin'; it is the paths, not the boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Public footpaths are rights of way across land, meant for walkers.

clue.text: Subject of article by Orlando

parts.note: the is the definite article
Orlando is this puzzle's setter, who refers to themself

explanation.surface: The setter names the topic of a piece they wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: Orlando is the setter's pseudonym, so the name stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or subject of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Where university education may lead? Not entirely

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: towards a qualification such as a BA
second meaning: partly, to some extent

explanation.surface: A doubtful comment on whether a university education really results in a qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to some extent, and literally names heading towards a university qualification.
